newsitem.title: USA: Ryder to slash 2,100 jobs, sell nearly 200 facilities.
newsitem.headline: Ryder to slash 2,100 jobs, sell nearly 200 facilities.

text.p: Truck leasing firm Ryder System Inc. said Monday it will slash about 2,100 jobs and dispose of nearly 200 facilities to cut costs and improve profits.

The company will take an unexpectedly large pretax charge of $215 million in the l996 fourth quarter for the actions, resulting in a net loss for the quarter and the full year. Executives of Miami, Fla.-based Ryder met with security analysts in New York on Monday.
Chairman M. Anthony Burns said in a statement that Ryder had taken a tough approach to assessing the businesses it wishes to pursue in the future.
It sold its famed yellow Ryder rental truck fleet in l996 and, as announced last October, is actively reviewing options for the future of its Automotive Carrier business.
Steps taken so far in the restructuring are expected to produce pretax savings of about $75 million in l997 and more than $150 million a year after that, it said.
About 700 employees have already taken advantage of a voluntary early retirement programme that was offered late last year as part of the restructuring, it said.
"Important as these savings are, the real heart of the programme is the structural change we have made in our leading lines of business," Burns said in a statement.
"We have put our integrated logistics and truck leasing and rental businesses in a position to succeed, and we will accept no less."
Most of the restructuring has already been completed and remaining actions will be completed during 1997, Ryder said.
Under the restructuring, Ryder will replace the truck leasing business' long-standing, 70-district field organisation with 10 vice presidents to oversee separate customer business units.
Ryder will move more than 80 percent of corporate staff positions to the new business units, which will have direct control over their administrative services.
The company will combine Ryder International and Ryder Integrated Logistics and realign the Logistics field organisation to focus more sharply on high-margin, knowledge-based services.
Ryder's stock edged up 37.5 cents to $29.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
